headline: Common Mistakes That Ruin a Guest Bathroom Remodel
articleBody:
Renovating a guest bathroom seems simple on the surface, but small footprints leave little margin for error. A few common missteps can leave visiting guests feeling cramped or leave you dealing with moisture troubles down the road.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Overlooking door swings and clearance: Installing a deeper vanity or an elongated toilet without checking the swing radius of the entry or linen closet door creates awkward daily traffic jams.
- Neglecting exterior ventilation: Relying on a weak fan or letting exhaust air vent into an unconditioned attic space traps steam, leading to mold and peeling paint.
- Choosing high-maintenance porous surfaces: Using unsealed natural stone or delicate surfaces in a secondary bath makes cleaning tough after busy holiday visitors depart.
- Failing to inspect rough plumbing before closing drywall: Skipping a thorough leak check on supply valves and drain traps before hanging board can conceal tiny drips that ruin new cabinetry.
- Skimping on practical storage: Leaving guests without dedicated space for toiletries, fresh towels, or hair dryers clutters the countertop immediately.

How to Compare Your Options
When planning your renovation, balance aesthetic goals with durable, easy-to-clean materials that stand up to humid conditions.
